title: Via launches two new services and expands a third service in New Jersey
summary: Westfield’s new RideUC and Camden and Gloucester Counties’ new CG Hopper service will see the expansion of microtransit across the state.
body_markdown:
On October 20, Union County and Via launched RideUC, an on-demand transit service that provides Westfield residents and visitors with a new way to reach jobs, schools, shopping, medical appointments, and nearby transit.


On October 28, Union County hosted an event at Westfield Train Station to celebrate the launch of RideUC.


“Our goal is to make it easier for Union County residents to get where they need to go without transportation being a barrier,” said Union County Commissioner Chairman Joseph C. Bodek. “RideUC is another way we’re investing in practical, affordable transportation that connects people to their communities and to the services they rely on. We’re proud to bring this pilot program to Westfield and look forward to seeing the difference it makes for residents.”


“As a Westfield resident and a mom of five, I know firsthand how much time families spend getting everyone where they need to be,” said Union County Commissioner Kimberly Palmieri-Mouded. “I have two children who are old enough to start getting around on their own, and having a service like RideUC gives families another option. Whether it’s getting downtown, meeting friends, or catching the train, it’s a convenient way to get around without always having to depend on someone for a ride. I’m especially excited to see this program come to my hometown.”


The launch caps off a busy month in the state of New Jersey, which also saw the launch of a new service in Camden and Gloucester Counties, CG Hopper, and an expansion of the highly successful Passaic Move service to the City of Paterson.


CG Hopper, a new on-demand service specifically designed for seniors and riders with disabilities, was launched in partnership with SCUCS, NJ TRANSIT, and Camden and Gloucester Counties to expand access to reliable, convenient transportation that helps residents maintain their independence and stay connected to their communities.


And finally, Passaic County expanded the Passaic MOVE service into Paterson. Since launching in May 2025 in Passaic and Clifton, Passaic MOVE has received a tremendous response from the community, with over 115k rides completed! With the expansion to Paterson, riders are able to travel within and between all three cities.


"We are thrilled to play such a pivotal role in bringing the next generation of public mobility to New Jersey,” said Via's Chief Revenue Officer, Michael Vaccarino. “Microtransit has proven to be a vital resource for these communities and we are delighted to expand access to social, economic, and healthcare opportunities for residents across the state."
